newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW--Sportmart sees Canada exit gains soon.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW--Sportmart sees Canada exit gains soon.

text.p: Sportmart Inc, which said it will post a loss for fiscal 1996 because of poor sales at its soon-to-close Canadian stores, said Friday it expects to see immediate improvements on its balance sheet.

"We should see improvements (to our balance sheet) in the first quarter," said Tom Hendrickson, Sportmart's chief financial officer, "simply because we won't have the losses from Canada and because of our increased ad spending."
Sportmart said Thursday it will exit Canada by closing 11 stores and taking a charge against earnings of between $18 million and $21 million after related income tax benefits.

The company declined to quantify the loss expected in the fourth quarter ended February 2. Sportmart, which reported net income of $0.12 a share for the nine months ended October 27, is scheduled to report year-end results in late March.

Sportmart said last fall the $0.12 per share profit for the first nine months of 1996 was made up of profits of $0.40 a share for U.S. operations and a loss of $0.28 a share for the Canadian operations.
The company also noted that same-store sales at its 11 Canadian units in November and December fell by 25 percent compared with the same two-month period one year ago.

"The Canadian retail market is very difficult, especially for sporting goods stores," explained N. Richard Nelson, a retail industry analyst at Nesbitt Burns. "The Toronto market is 'overstored' with more than 20 superstores in the area. Nobody is doing well there at all."
Nelson said Sportmart's decision to exit Candaa will eliminate its losses in that market.

Sportmart President Mike Scott said Friday the company's new refocus on U.S. operations will include stepped up advertising efforts and a move forward on its "Four Worlds" retailing concept. The strategy brings together soft goods, like fitness apparel, with hard goods like treadmills, Scott said.
Scott said Sportmart will have between three and five "Four Worlds" stores in operation in California by the end of 1997.

"This is a four-to-five-year plan. We'll spend 13 percent more on advertising for our California stores this year, and devote about nine percent to promote our frequent-buyer program," Scott said in an interview.
He added that future expansion plans will depend on how well the refocus affects sales.
"We will accelerate our growth strategy based on positive sales results," Scott said.
Shares of Sportmart were off 11/16 to 3-3/8.
